title: The Shor Code
summary: Shor's nine-qubit code concatenates the phase-flip and bit-flip codes and corrects an arbitrary error on one qubit.
objectives: Build the nine-qubit Shor code by concatenating the phase-flip and bit-flip codes
Decode with majority votes inside each block and then across the block leaders
Show that correcting X, Y and Z on one qubit also corrects an arbitrary single-qubit error
Predict which two-qubit errors the code turns into a logical error
mission: Protect qubit 0 against any error on a single qubit of the nine. Complete encode(): a phase-flip code on the block leaders 0, 3 and 6, then a bit-flip code inside each block (0, 1, 2), (3, 4, 5) and (6, 7, 8). Complete decode(): undo the bit-flip codes with a majority vote in each block, then undo the phase-flip code with a majority vote on the leaders. Afterwards qubit 0 must hold the input state again after an X, Y or Z error on any one of the nine qubits, and after an arbitrary rotation on any one qubit, for any input state.

prediction.question: X errors hit qubits 0 and 1, both in the first block. What does the Shor code do?
options: It corrects them, because the two flips are in the same block
It fails: the block decoding also flips qubit 2, and X on all three qubits of a block is a logical Z
It fails: the syndrome is 00, so the errors are not detected
prediction.explanation: Inside a block, two bit flips have the syndrome of a flip on the third qubit, so the block decoding applies X to qubit 2 and X⊗X⊗X is left acting on the block. This operator leaves |000⟩ + |111⟩ unchanged and multiplies |000⟩ − |111⟩ by −1. On the logical states it gives |0_L⟩ → |0_L⟩ and |1_L⟩ → −|1_L⟩, a logical Z. The code corrects any error on one qubit, not two.

hints: Encoding has two layers. First the phase-flip code on the leaders: qml.CNOT(wires=[0, 3]), qml.CNOT(wires=[0, 6]), then qml.Hadamard on wires 0, 3 and 6. Then, for each block (a, b, c), the bit-flip code: qml.CNOT(wires=[a, b]) and qml.CNOT(wires=[a, c]).

Decode in the reverse order. For each block (a, b, c): qml.CNOT(wires=[a, b]), qml.CNOT(wires=[a, c]), qml.Toffoli(wires=[b, c, a]). Afterwards the leader holds the block's bit with a bit flip corrected, and a phase flip anywhere in the block has become a phase flip of the leader.

The leaders 0, 3 and 6 now form a phase-flip code. Apply qml.Hadamard to each, then repeat the majority vote: qml.CNOT(wires=[0, 3]), qml.CNOT(wires=[0, 6]), qml.Toffoli(wires=[3, 6, 0]). Qubit 0 then holds |ψ⟩.
